rendered: The premise is not supported by the document: prestraining did not lower the Li-ion diffusion coefficient of the V2O5 films. It raised it. The strained films show a diffusion coefficient increased to about 2.5-times[1] the unstrained value, which is the enhancement the paper reports (up to 2.5-times[2] for applied strains below 2%[3]). The stated mechanism is that an out-of-plane compressive strain produces in-plane tensile strains: An out of plane compressive strain results[4] in in-plane tensile strains, which effectively increase the total[5] volume of the crystal, and with Poisson's ratio a net positive volume change is expected in the film. The authors attribute the increase to reduction of ion migration barriers[6], which imposed mechanical strains can achieve.
